item.title: Krzy\.{z}'s conjecture for the seventh coefficient
item.description: arXiv:2611.00397v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A holomorphic function bounded in modulus by one in the unit disk has Taylor coefficients of modulus at most one. If the function has no zeros, Krzy\.{z}'s conjecture predicts the stronger bound $2/e$ for every coefficient of positive order. We establish this bound for the seventh coefficient: $|a_7|\leq2/e$, with equality precisely for the functions $\eta\exp[-(1-\xi z^7)/(1+\xi z^7)]$, where $|\eta|=|\xi|=1$. Thus the largest possible value of $|f^{(7)}(0)|$ in this class is $7!\,2/e$, and the extremal functions are uniquely determined up to rotations of the variable and multiplication by a constant of modulus one.
item.dc:creator: Xiaohui Xie

item.title: Strongly Pseudoconvex Domains with Finite Dimensional $p$-Bergman Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.00501v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that for every $n\ge2$, $p>2$, and positive integer $m$, there exists a finite-volume pseudoconvex domain $D\subset\mathbb C^n$ with real-analytic strongly pseudoconvex boundary whose $p$-Bergman space $A^p(D)$ has dimension $m$. These domains admit smooth strictly plurisubharmonic exhaustions and satisfy $H^\infty(D)=\mathbb C$ and $\dim A^s(D)=\infty$ for every $0<s\le2$. Moreover, for every finite $s\ge p$, we have $\dim A^s(D)=\lceil pm/s\rceil$. As an application, we show that the Bergman projection fails to map $\mathcal{C}_c^\infty(D)$ into $A^p(D)$ and admits no bounded extension to $L^s(D)$ or $L^{s/(s-1)}(D)$ for any finite $s\ge p$.
item.dc:creator: Shreedhar Bhat, Soumya Ganguly, Achinta Kumar Nandi

item.title: Harmonic Quasiconformal Mappings in the BMO-Teichm\"uller space
item.description: arXiv:2611.00860v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\text{HQS}(\mathbb{R})$ denote the class of increasing homeomorphisms of the real line $\mathbb{R}$ that admit harmonic quasiconformal extensions to the upper half-plane $\mathbb{H}$. Kalaj and Pavlovi\'c proved that a homeomorphism $h$ belongs to $\text{HQS}(\mathbb{R})$ if and only if $h$ is bi-Lipschitz and the Hilbert transform of $h'$ belongs to $L^\infty(\mathbb{R})$, and asked whether $\text{HQS}(\mathbb{R})$ is a group under composition. We give a negative answer to this question. Further, we show that the Beltrami coefficients of harmonic quasiconformal mappings of $\mathbb{H}$ can be identified with the open unit ball of $H^\infty(\mathbb{H})$. Finally, we study the topology of $\text{HQS}(\mathbb{R})$ and prove that it is contractible in the topology inherited from the BMO-Teichm\"uller space.
item.dc:creator: Liu Tailiang, Shen Yuliang

item.title: Modulus of Continuity for Finite Energy Homeomorphisms of the Circle
item.description: arXiv:2611.00904v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given $h_o: \mathbb{S} \to \mathbb{S}$, an orientation-preserving homeomorphism of the unit circle, we seek to establish very weak conditions so as to derive a modulus of continuity for $h_o$ and its inverse $h_o^{-1}$, then use these to derive various compactness properties for families of circle homeomorphisms and solutions to Beltrami equations.
item.dc:creator: Mihai Florincescu, Gaven Martin, Cong Yao

item.title: Stein Criteria for Holomorphic Fibre Bundles
item.description: arXiv:2611.01693v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study Steinness of holomorphic fibre bundles. Over a compact Riemann surface, we prove that every holomorphic ball bundle is weakly $1$-complete and that its total space is Stein if and only if it admits no holomorphic section. We also obtain higher-dimensional Stein criteria for reductive ball bundles and affine bundles in terms of positivity of the canonical class. A topological obstruction to the $1$-convexity of holomorphic fibre bundles is also established.
item.dc:creator: Masakazu Takakura

item.title: Entire solutions of Fermat-Type Partial Differential-Difference equations in higher dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2611.01931v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The purpose of this paper is to investigate the finite-order entire solutions of the following Fermat-type partial differential-difference equations: \begin{align*} (P_1(z)f(z+c))^{m_1}+\left(P_2(z)f(z)+\sideset{}{_{j=1}^m}{\sum} Q_j(z)\partial_{z_j}(f(z))\right)^{m_2}=P(z), \end{align*} \begin{align*} (P_1(z)f(z))^{m_1}+\left(P_2(z)f(z+c)+\sideset{}{_{j=1}^m}{\sum} Q_j(z)\partial_{z_j}(f(z))\right)^{m_2}=P(z) \end{align*} and \begin{align*} \left(\sideset{}{_{j=1}^m}{\sum} Q_j(z)\partial_{z_j}(f(z))\right)^{m_1}+\left(P_1(z)f(z+c)+P_2(z)f(z)\right)^{m_2}=P(z), \end{align*} in $\mathbb{C}^m$, where $m_1,m_2\in\mathbb{N}$ such that $m_1+m_2>2$, $c=(c_1,c_2,\ldots,c_m)\in\mathbb{C}^m$, $P(\not\equiv 0)$, $P_1$, $P_2$ and $Q_i\;(i=1,2,\ldots,m)$ are polynomials in $\mathbb{C}^m$ such that $P(z)$ is irreducible in $\mathbb{C}^m$. The results established in this paper generalize those of Xu et al. \cite{Xu-Luo-Cao-2025} from $\mathbb{C}$ to $\mathbb{C}^m$.
item.dc:creator: Sujoy Majumder, Jhilik Banerjee, Abhijit Banerjee, Elias Saleeby

item.title: Polynomial convexity and non-polynomial convexity of totally real discs in $\mathbb{C}^2$
item.description: arXiv:2611.02004v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the polynomial convexity of smooth totally real discs contained in the boundaries of strongly pseudoconvex domains in $\mathbb{C}^2$. Using Wermer's classical example, we construct a bounded domain with smooth strongly pseudoconvex boundary containing a non-polynomially convex totally real disc. We also construct a nonsingular Levi-flat hypersurface in a non-Runge domain containing such a disc. This provides a partial negative answer, to a conjecture proposed in an earlier work. Furthermore, we prove that the Wermer graph over the closed disc of radius $R$ is polynomially convex for every $R\in (0,1)$. Finally, we establish a sufficient condition for the polynomial convexity of totally real discs contained in the smoothly bounded strongly pseudoconvex domains in $\mathbb{C}^2$.
item.dc:creator: Golam Mostafa Mondal

item.title: Zero sets in spaces of analytic functions with $p$-summable Taylor coefficients
item.description: arXiv:2611.02159v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A zero set for a space of analytic functions is a set on which some nonzero function in the space vanishes; it is exact if it coincides with the full zero set of such a function. We construct zero sets that are not exact in the classical coefficient spaces $\ell_A^p$ of functions analytic on the unit disk for every $1\le p<2$. For $1<p<2$, a single Blaschke set $W$ is a zero set for every $\ell_A^p$ in this range, but is not exact for any of them. The endpoint case $p=1$, corresponding to the analytic Wiener algebra $\ell_A^1$, requires a separate construction, yielding a non-exact zero set that accumulates at only one point of the unit circle. The proofs combine quadratic characters, finite-dimensional Clark transforms, and logarithmic estimates in zero-free regions. We also establish sharp moment duality and an exact summability criterion for a family of regular polygons. For $p>2$, we construct two disjoint exact zero sets whose union is a uniqueness set. For these exponents, suitably chosen rotations also yield a continuum-sized family of nonzero closed shift-invariant subspaces of $\ell^p$ with pairwise trivial intersections, recovering a known existence result.
item.dc:creator: Evgeny Abakumov, Isabelle Chalendar, Alexei Poltoratski

item.title: Schwarz Lemma in Quaternionic Setting and $\mathbb C^4$
item.dc:creator: Chris Connell, Matvei Libine

item.title: Monotonicity and bounded variation for harmonic mappings with applications to special functions
item.description: arXiv:2611.02290v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate sufficient conditions for the close-to-convexity and univalence of planar harmonic mappings. First, we establish a unified monotonicity criterion for harmonic mappings that incorporates the ordinary and odd harmonic cases. We then develop a criterion based on the total variation of successive coefficient differences. Unlike conventional monotonicity conditions, this approach allows the coefficient sequences to exhibit non-monotone behavior. Several previously established criteria for harmonic close-to-convexity are recovered as particular consequences. Applications are developed for harmonic mappings associated with Gaussian hypergeometric functions and Legendre polynomials, with explicit restrictions on their parameters.
item.dc:creator: Jugal Kishore Prajapat

item.title: Improved criteria for geometric properties of confluent hypergeometric functions
item.description: arXiv:2611.02298v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we establish sufficient conditions for several geometric properties of confluent hypergeometric functions. Using differential subordination techniques, we derive parameter conditions ensuring lower bounds for the real part of the confluent hypergeometric function and sectorial subordination of its derivative. We also obtain criteria for strong convexity and strong starlikeness of prescribed order. In addition, we investigate the close-to-convexity and starlikeness of the confluent hypergeometric functions. Particular cases yield corresponding results for generalized Laguerre polynomials. The obtained criteria are compared with existing sufficient conditions, and their implications for the geometric theory of special functions are discussed.
item.dc:creator: Jugal Kishore Prajapat Naveen Kumari

item.title: Meromorphic functions together with their partial derivatives sharing zeros and poles in $\mathbb{C}^m$
item.description: arXiv:2611.02682v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the paper, using Nevanlinna's value distribution theory of meromorphic functions in $\mathbb{C}^m$, we study the problem: Let $f$ and $g$ be two finite order non-constant meromorphic functions in $\mathbb{C}^m$ such that $f$ and $g$ share $0$ and $\infty$ CM. If $\partial_{z_i}(f)$ and $\partial_{z_i}(g)$ share $0$ CM and if for one $n>1$, $\partial^n_{z_i}(f)$ and $\partial^n_{z_i}(g)$ share $0$ CM, where $i=1,2,\ldots,m$, then $f$ and $g$ have special presentations. Our finding extends the result of K\"{o}hler (Meromorphic functions sharing zeros and poles and also some of their derivatives sharing zeros, Complex Var., 11 (1989), 39-48) into higher dimensions. Moreover, we show by an example that the restriction on the growth of $f$ and $g$ is necessary.
item.dc:creator: Hong Yan Xu, Sujoy Majumder, Goutam Haldar

item.title: Characterization of the boundary zero set of stable polynomials in $\mathbb B_2$
item.description: arXiv:2611.02838v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given a polynomial $p\in \mathbb{C}[z,w]$ whose zeros lie outside the unit ball $\mathbb{B}_2$ of $\mathbb{C}^2,$ we study its local Weierstrass polynomial--obtained via the Weierstrass Preparation Theorem--and provide a strong version of the Nash curve selection lemma. These results lead to a characterization of the intersection of the zero set of $p$ with the unit sphere: $\mathcal{Z}(p)\cap\mathbb{S}_{2}.$
item.dc:creator: Dimitrios Vavitsas

item.title: Corona and Gleason problems for certain Banach spaces of holomorphic functions
item.description: arXiv:2611.02949v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We use a combination of the classical dead-end space method and the interpolation (by bounded holomorphic functions) method to affirmatively solve Corona and Gleason problems for familiar Banach spaces of holomorphic functions such as (Besov-)Lipschitz spaces of holomorphic functions on bounded symmetric domains (including the unit ball and polydisc) in $\mathbb{C}^n$, holomorphic mean (Besov-)Lipschitz spaces, (Besov-)Hardy-Sobolev spaces and some special classes of holomorphic mixed-norm (Bergman) spaces (including weighted Bergman spaces) as well as some special classes of holomorphic (mean) Besov-Lipschitz spaces on the unit ball in $\mathbb{C}^n$. Indeed, we extend our recent work on both problems for holomorphic Lipschitz algebras.
item.dc:creator: S. R. Patel

item.title: Failure of bounded $\bar\partial$-solvability on pseudoconvex domains of finite type
item.description: arXiv:2611.03127v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that for every integer $n\ge3$ there is a bounded pseudoconvex domain in $\mathbb{C}^n$ with smooth real-analytic boundary whose maximum boundary D'Angelo $1$-type is $16$, carrying a $\bar\partial$-closed form continuous on the closure and smooth in the domain with no bounded distributional solution. On each fixed domain, we also construct a uniformly bounded sequence of smooth $\bar\partial$-closed data for which every bounded solution has norm at least $ck^{1/320}$ for all sufficiently large $k$. Each datum in this sequence and a corresponding solution extend smoothly to a neighborhood of the closure. The obstruction comes from a singular curve in two weak complex tangential directions, whose normalization admits holomorphic functions that do not extend to a neighborhood of the curve.
item.dc:creator: Yun-Heng Du

item.title: Weakly Lipschitz mappings in higher dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2611.03532v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce and investigate the main features of weakly Lipschitz mappings whose pointwise Lipschitz constant is controlled from above by the derivative of a set function. The main results give conditions under which such mappings belong to $W^{1,n}_{\rm loc},$ and show that the class contains metrically quasiconformal mappings as a proper subclass. In addition, under a Rado--Reichelderfer type oscillation assumption, we derive diameter control, image-measure bounds, sufficient conditions for Lusin's $(N)$-property, and an area formula.
item.dc:creator: Anatoly Golberg

item.title: A Koszul-Type Splitting Theorem for Complex Supermanifolds
item.description: arXiv:2611.00331v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the splitting problem for complex supermanifolds using formal exponential maps and Ehresmann connections. We show that every formal exponential map induces a splitting of the underlying supermanifold. Furthermore, we establish that every Ehresmann connection determines a linearization of the infinite jet space, extending the corresponding construction for ordinary manifolds to supermanifolds. For Ehresmann connections preserving the zero section, we construct a formal exponential map in two ways: via the linearization of the infinite jet space and directly from the connection operator. We prove that both constructions yield the same map and induce the same splitting, thereby generalizing Koszul's splitting theorem from linear connections to zero-section-preserving Ehresmann connections. Finally, we provide examples showing that, without this assumption, the two constructions may yield different splittings, or one or both of them may fail to induce a splitting.
item.dc:creator: Luiz F. A. Campos, Alexey Sharapov, Elizaveta Vishnyakova

item.title: On the Local Regularity of Homogeneous Complex Monge-Amp\`ere Equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.00736v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish a local higher regularity theorem for the homogeneous complex Monge-Ampere equation on $X\times D$, where $X$ is a complete, possibly noncompact Kahler manifold and $D\subset\mathbb C$ is the unit disc. For a bounded weak solution given by the Perron envelope, we prove higher regularity on a smaller spatial domain when the smooth boundary data are locally small. The geometric hypotheses require uniformly convex local Kahler potentials and a local barrier threshold sufficiently large relative to the global $L^\infty$ bound of the solution. We also obtain quantitative local Holder estimates. The proof combines a perturbative construction of local holomorphic disc foliations with a construction of global subsolutions using convexity and barriers. A key analytic difficulty is the loss of Holder regularity in the construction of holomorphic disc families, which we address using BMO estimates and Nash-Moser-Zehnder theorems. Comparison along the discs identifies the local smooth solution by holomorphic discs foliation with the global weak solution. We apply the theorem and its proof to compact Kahler manifolds and to ALE, ALF, and asymptotically complex hyperbolic (ACH) ends. Under the stated geometric and decay assumptions, we obtain higher regularity of each prescribed order sufficiently far out, together with weighted Holder estimates preserving the boundary decay.
item.dc:creator: Qi Yao

item.title: Spatial degeneracy along weak geodesics in the space of K\"ahler potentials
item.description: arXiv:2611.00744v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study spatial Hessian degeneracy along weak K\"ahler geodesics. We construct examples in three settings: (1) On every compact K\"ahler manifold, the spatial form degenerates on a nonempty open set during an interior time interval, although both endpoints are smooth and strictly K\"ahler. (2) On ALE K\"ahler manifolds with a holomorphic quotient end and a decaying potential to the Euclidean metric, spatial degeneracy occurs on open regions arbitrarily far along an unbounded horn. (3) For cone and Poincar\'e endpoint metrics along a smooth divisor, normal spatial degeneracy occurs on open sets approaching the divisor. Both cone endpoints retain the prescribed angle. The first construction answers negatively the spatial-positivity question recorded in Darvas's survey. The ALE and divisor constructions show that weak geodesics need not preserve the asymptotic behavior of the endpoint metrics.
item.dc:creator: Xia Xiao, Qi Yao

item.title: Functions of $\boldsymbol{S}_p$-almost commuting unitary operators and contractions. An extension of the Carey--Pincus trace formula
item.description: arXiv:2611.01149v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper we study functions of pairs of unitary operators and pairs of contractions with commutators in the Schatten-von Neumann class $\boldsymbol{S}_p$. We obtain commutator estimates and prove that our functional calculus is multiplicative modulo $\boldsymbol{S}_p$. On the other hand, we show that our commutator estimates do not extend to the case $p>2$. We also obtain an extension of the Carey--Pincus trace formula. The main tool of this paper is a technique of triple operator integrals.
item.dc:creator: A. B. Aleksandrov, V. V. Peller

item.title: Hodge theory and topology of Bogomolov--Guan manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2611.01210v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Bogomolov--Guan manifolds are simply connected, irreducible holomorphic symplectic manifolds that are not K\"ahler, yet they echo hyperk\"ahler geometry in striking ways. We show that their Fr\"olicher spectral sequence degenerates at $E_1$ and that their Hodge numbers are stable under small deformations. The general fibers of their natural Lagrangian fibration are rationally null-homologous, and the Beauville--Bogomolov--Fujiki form is degenerate. Despite this, in every dimension, the Euler characteristics agree with those of generalized Kummer manifolds. In dimensions four and six, we compute the full Hodge diamonds and all Chern and Pontryagin numbers. Surprisingly, these characteristic numbers are the same as the generalized Kummer ones, even though the Betti numbers differ and the Hodge diamonds are asymmetric.
item.dc:creator: Nikon Kurnosov, \'Angel David R\'ios Ortiz

item.title: Stochastic Euler Products in the Paley-Wiener Space
item.description: arXiv:2611.01347v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: General sufficient conditions, in terms of stochastic Euler products, are given for a realization of a point process to have finite excess or finite deficiency in the Paley-Wiener space.
item.dc:creator: Alexander I. Bufetov

item.title: A general framework for universal bounds on the analytic functional calculus
item.description: arXiv:2611.01503v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish a general principle for bounding the matrix-valued analytic functional calculus $F\mapsto F(T)$ of a Hilbert space operator $T$, independently of the matrix size. It rests on two properties of an auxiliary Hilbert space of holomorphic functions: the accretivity of its moment map at $T$ and a uniform bound for its multipliers. The mechanism of OpenAI's direct proof of the complete Crouzeix conjecture is the instance in which these properties come from the positivity of the double-layer potential and from norm estimates for Faber series of a convex domain. The main advantage of our method is that the auxiliary space can be chosen freely, to fit the class of operators, and a well-chosen space can give sharp constants, also on domains that are not convex, simply connected or bounded. On every intersection of two disks of the Riemann sphere, for operators with both closed disks as spectral sets, we obtain a complete bound independent of the two disks, which is sharp for the quantum annulus and the strip. For operators, bounded or m-sectorial, with numerical range in a sector, our bounds improve on the complete Crouzeix inequality for every opening; they are optimal for the right angle, answering a question of Crouzeix, and nearly optimal for acute angles. On Jordan domains with regular real-analytic boundary, a space built from the exterior conformal map and the Faber polynomials of the domain gives complete bounds for operators whose double-layer potential is bounded below. They are optimal for the disk, recover the complete Crouzeix inequality on convex domains, and improve on earlier bounds, including bounds of Crouzeix and Greenbaum, also on nonconvex domains.
item.dc:creator: Mihai Putinar, Georgios Tsikalas

item.title: Transfer of similarity to Hilbert space contractions through inner functions: a proof of Douglas's conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2611.01703v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $A$ be a bounded operator on a Hilbert space and let $u$ be a non-constant Blaschke product, finite or infinite. We prove that if the spectrum of $A$ does not meet the closure of the set of poles of $u$, then $u(A)$ is similar to a contraction if and only if $A$ is. This settles a conjecture of R.G. Douglas. For infinite products $u$, no additional condition on the zeros beyond the Blaschke condition is required. We also show that '$u(A)$ is similar to a contraction if and only if $A$ is' for all non-constant inner functions $u$ whose reflected singularity set, the closure of the set of poles together with the singular support, avoids the spectrum of $A$. We also prove a weighted resolvent version of the theorem, which allows the poles to accumulate on the spectrum to a limited extent; a column criterion for partial products, which is shown to force their norm convergence; and a simultaneous version for commuting tuples of operators tested by separated inner functions sharing one Lyapunov operator. For finite Blaschke products we obtain a polynomial form of the Lyapunov operator, which gives an estimate for the similarity constants. We also characterise the tuples of finite Blaschke products that form a uniform strong test collection: they are exactly the tuples that are injective, with non-vanishing joint derivative, on the closed disc. Finally, we show by examples that the separation hypothesis cannot be replaced by the existence of a bounded $H^\infty$ calculus, by the existence of a norm radial limit, or by the strong convergence of the partial products, even for Ritt operators.
item.dc:creator: Catalin Badea

item.title: Calabi flow on polarized K\"ahler surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.01968v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study global smooth Calabi flows on polarized K\"ahler surfaces $(M,L)$, assuming uniformly bounded Sobolev constants and the algebraic conditions $\chi(\mathcal O_M)=1$ and $c_1(M)\cdot c_1(L)>0$. Using the orbifold compactness theorem, we prove a uniform Bergman estimate, construct a normal test configuration for each geometric limit, and establish uniqueness of the extremal orbifold limit up to polarized holomorphic isometry. K-polystability then identifies the limit with the original surface and gives a constant scalar curvature K\"ahler metric. We also prove finite-group equivariant versions of these results. Independently of the flow, we obtain a uniform Bergman lower bound for polarized cscK surfaces with bounded volume and Sobolev constants and $|S|\leq1$. We illustrate the hypotheses with nonstationary flows near a product cscK metric on $\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^1$ and near Calabi's non-cscK extremal metric on the first Hirzebruch surface. Their controlled-cone energy inequalities follow from elementary calculations and continuity.
item.dc:creator: Haozhao Li, Bing Wang, Kai Zheng

item.title: Generalized Quasi-Symmetric Nets: A Constructive Approach to the Equimodular Elliptic Type and to Flexible $m \times n$ Nets
item.description: arXiv:2611.02229v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quadrilateral meshes that flex with rigid planar faces are of interest to transformable architecture, rigid-foldable origami, and mechanical metamaterials. Their building blocks are flexible $3 \times 3$ nets, that is, Kokotsakis polyhedra with a quadrangular base, classified by Izmestiev. We study one of his types, the equimodular elliptic type, defined by three conditions on the flat angles, the third of them through Jacobi elliptic functions. We turn these conditions into equivalent algebraic ones, free of elliptic functions, which lead to the generalized quasi-symmetric nets (GQS-nets), polyhedra of this type that include the known elliptic quasi-symmetric nets. For every polyhedron of this type, we give a flexible polyhedron with the same flat angles and its flexion in closed form. From the simplest GQS-nets, we assemble arbitrarily large flexible $m \times n$ nets. Examples include nets that, at one position, form letters; further nets in the supplementary materials form digits or, seen along their rows, approximately follow the side silhouettes of a bunny and a fish. Unlike numerically computed mechanisms, these nets are exactly flexible. As an application, we design three such nets as transportable arch halls of 80 mm sandwich panels, which fold to fit through the door of a standard container or into the well of a low-bed semi-trailer, and we check them numerically under snow load and build a 1:20 model of one. Supplementary Mathematica notebooks verify the symbolic computations, a Python tool constructs the nets and checks them numerically, including for self-intersections, and further scripts recheck the halls.
item.dc:creator: Abdukhomid Nurmatov, Florian Rist, Jonathan Klein, Dominik L. Michels

item.title: Limiting properties of Hermitian-Einstein metrics under variation of the K\"ahler class
item.description: arXiv:2611.03025v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the behaviour of Hermitian-Einstein metrics on a holomorphic vector bundle over a compact K\"ahler manifold, as the underlying K\"ahler metric varies and its K\"ahler class changes. In particular, if the bundle stops being stable at some point, the Hermitian-Einstein metrics blow up, and their rescaling can be used to construct a destabilizing subsheaf, following the argument of Uhlenbeck and Yau. Furthermore, we study the behaviour of Chern connections of these metrics, and show, that after passing to a subsequence, and applying suitable gauge transforms these connections converge, and identify the blow-up locus of their Uhlenbeck limit.
item.dc:creator: Nikita Klemyatin

item.title: Rigidity of the Peres-Vir\'ag class
item.description: arXiv:2611.03118v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Consider the hyperbolic Gaussian analytic function (GAF) \begin{equation*} F_{\mathbb{D}}(z)=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty }\xi _{n}z^{n},\qquad |z|<1, \end{equation*} where the $\xi _{n}$ are independent standard complex Gaussian variables. Peres-Vir\'{a}g theorem tells that the distribution of the zeros of $F_{\mathbb{D}}(z)$ is provided by a Determinantal Point Process (DPP). We prove that $F_{\mathbb{D}}(z)$ is the only GAF whose zeros are determinantal with a Hermitian kernel, up to multiplication by a zero-free holomorphic function and a one-to-one holomorphic change of variable, with a \ non-degeneracy condition imposed to exclude trivial cases. The proof identifies a geometric property of GAF's with (local) determinantal zeros: the metric defined by the first intensity must have constant curvature $-4$.
item.dc:creator: Lu\'is Daniel Abreu

item.title: Human Variations on AI Mathematics
item.description: arXiv:2611.03225v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This article is motivated by the OpenAI manuscripts "Minimal metrics and interior injectivity for nef adjoints" and "Log abundance in characteristic zero". We establish a jet comparison for metrics with minimal singularities and use it to prove a dlt-type extension theorem. Combined with geometric arguments from the latter manuscript, this yields an alternative analytic proof of its Theorem~3.1.
item.dc:creator: Junyan Cao, Mihai Paun

item.title: Atomic decomposition of Bergman-Orlicz space on the upper complex half-plane
item.description: arXiv:2503.23570v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this work, we propose an atomic decomposition of the Bergman-Orlicz spaces on the complex upper half-plane. Using this result, we characterize Carleson embeddings with loss between Bergman-Orlicz spaces and certain Orlicz spaces. We also leverage this last result to control the composition operator between two Bergman-Orlicz spaces.
item.dc:creator: J. M. Tanoh Dje, Beno\^it. F. Sehba

item.title: Dirichlet symbols and the nonlinear wave equation
item.description: arXiv:2608.04666v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop the geometry of conformal mappings through Dirichlet operator symbols and the nonlinear wave equation. These symbols, introduced in the work of Hedenmalm and Shimorin (2020), are holomorphic functions on the bidisk associated with contractions on $L^2(\mathbb{D})$. For Grunsky operators, the nonlinear wave equation and the related Riccati equation induce a hierarchy of of differential relations along the diagonal. We use this jet hierachy to obtain alternative coordinates and a characterization of the manifold $\Sigma/\mathbb{C}$ of normalized exterior univalent functions modulo translations, without an explicit univalence test. This manifold may be viewed as an extension of the universal Teichm\"uller space beyond the quasicircle boundary setting. The diagonal jets also give rise to a hierarchy of \emph{diagonal series Schwarzian derivatives}. Already the fourth Schwarzian $S_4(\psi)$ leads to differential equations connected with the Weierstrass elliptic $\wp$ function and Painlev\'e I, revealing a comparison between the geometry of conformal mappings and that of complex tori. As a quantitative application of the framework, we interpret asymptotic variance through the Littlewood-Paley formula as an asymptotic density of quadratic nonlinearity energy under logarithmic averaging. We introduce Schwarzian asymptotic variance and obtain the upper bound $12.566563\ldots$ for its averaged squared hyperbolically normalized amplitude, in comparison with the classical pointwise bound $36$.
item.dc:creator: Ramlal Debnath, Haakan Hedenmalm

item.title: Carleson measures, Volterra integral operators and multipliers for $Q_K$ spaces
item.description: arXiv:2608.20205v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study embeddings and operators on the M\"obius-invariant spaces $Q_K$ using two dyadic capacities. One capacity is defined by analytic packets; the other is defined by domination of positive semidefinite matrices. We prove that they are equivalent. They give criteria for bounded and compact embeddings $Q_K\to L^2(\mu)$, bounded and compact Volterra operators, and pointwise multipliers. For the weights $K(t)=t^p/\log^\beta(e/t)$, $0<p<1$ and $\beta\ge1$, we prove $\mathcal M(Q_K)\subsetneq H^\infty\cap Q_K^{\log}.$ This disproves the logarithmic multiplier conjecture recorded in Bao and Wulan's 2021 survey.
item.dc:creator: Wujun Cao, Zhouyuan Jiang, Songxiao Li

item.title: Proof of the generalized Chui conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2609.03134v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove Chui's conjecture on sums of Cauchy kernels. It states that among all configurations of Cauchy kernels on the unit disk, the equispaced one minimizes $L^1$ norm of the sum in the unit disk. Moreover, we obtain a generalization to a wider set of functionals, including weighted $L^p$ norms for $p > 1$ with radially symmetric weights.
item.dc:creator: Egor Bezrukov

item.title: Multipliers and weighted d-bar estimates
item.description: arXiv:math/9912139v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study some size estimates for the solution of the equation d-bar u=f in one variable. The new ingredient is the use of holomorphic functions with precise growth restrictions in the construction of explicit solutions to the equation.
item.dc:creator: Joaquim Ortega-Cerda (University of Barcelona)

item.title: The Complete Intersection Discrepancy of a Curve II: Families of Curves
item.description: arXiv:2310.16558v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study equisingularity of families of reduced curves over smooth parameter spaces of arbitrary positive dimension, using the difference between two analytic invariants of a curve singularity: the multiplicity of its Jacobian ideal and its complete intersection discrepancy. This difference provides a fiberwise multiplicity criterion for Whitney equisingularity. We prove that Whitney equisingularity (equivalently, strong simultaneous resolution) is characterized by equidimensionality of the fibers of the exceptional locus of either the relative conormal space or the relative Nash blowup. We further show that this condition is equivalent to the emptiness of the relative polar variety of smallest dimension. In addition, we establish that the Milnor number of a reduced curve is Zariski upper semicontinuous. As an application, we show that the constancy of the Milnor number in a family of reduced curves is equivalent to its topological equisingularity, under a natural assumption on the fibers.
item.dc:creator: Andrei Bengu\c{s}-Lasnier, Terence Gaffney, Antoni Rangachev

item.title: Additive processes on the real line and Loewner chains
item.description: arXiv:2412.18742v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper investigates additive processes with respect to several different independences in non-commutative probability in terms of the convolution hemigroups of the distributions of the increments of the processes. In particular, we focus on the relation of monotone convolution hemigroups and Loewner chains, a special kind of family of conformal mappings, on the upper half-plane. Generalizing the celebrated Loewner differential equation, we formulate an integral equation and the concept of ``generator'' for any Loewner chain of reciprocal Cauchy transforms. This generalization enables us to remove the assumption of the absolute continuity of Loewner chains which had been imposed in the literature. The locally uniform convergence of Loewner chains is then equivalent to a suitable convergence of generators. Using generators, we define homeomorphisms between the aforementioned class of Loewner chains, the set of monotone convolution hemigroups, and the set of classical convolution hemigroups on the real line. We also discuss similar homeomorphisms to free, boolean and anti-monotone convolution hemigroups on the real line.
item.dc:creator: Takahiro Hasebe, Ikkei Hotta, Takuya Murayama

item.title: Understanding entropy using Aubin--Yau deformations
item.description: arXiv:2610.21198v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper we investigate three types of entropy that frequently appear in the research of K\"ahler geometry: the classical K\"ahler entropy, the radial entropy and the non-Archimedean entropy. We give a unifying interpretation for these entropies by showing that they can all be expressed as the derivative of the Monge--Amp\`ere energy along certain Aubin--Yau type deformations. Such considerations also lead to a novel algebraic criterion for the existence of constant scalar curvature K\"ahler metrics.
item.dc:creator: Tam\'as Darvas, Kewei Zhang

item.title: Higher-order sum rules for zeros of the planar Gaussian entire function
item.description: arXiv:2610.23697v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For each fixed integer $k\ge2$, we prove that integrating one coordinate of the truncated correlation of order $k$ for zeros of the planar Gaussian entire function (GEF) gives $-(k-1)$ times the truncated correlation of order $k-1$. The integral converges absolutely, and the identity holds pointwise, including at coincident fixed coordinates by continuous extension. This answers the marginal-identity part of Krishnapur and Yogeshwaran's question for the planar GEF. We also prove a general criterion for simple point processes: under local moment and absolute integrability assumptions, the identities hold almost everywhere if there are compactly supported cutoffs between zero and one, eventually equal to one on each compact set, whose linear statistics have variances tending to zero. For GEF zeros, strong clustering and variance bounds for smooth linear statistics verify these assumptions. The proof combines a mixed-cumulant estimate with the partition formula for ordinary and factorial cumulants.
item.dc:creator: Xiaolin Zhu, Feng Guo

item.title: Spectral Structures on Vector Bundles
item.description: arXiv:2610.38972v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop an intrinsic theory of spectral structures on holomorphic vector bundles over compact Riemann surfaces, generalising eigenspace decompositions without eigenvalues. Their geometric realisations are presentations of vector bundles as pushforwards of line bundles along finite branched covers. We construct their analytic moduli stack locally of finite presentation and identify it with the relative Picard stack of the universal family of finite covers. We prove that the forgetful morphism to the stack of vector bundles is representable by analytic spaces and is smooth and surjective on a distinguished smooth open substack. Consequently, every holomorphic family of vector bundles locally admits spectral presentations along smooth connected simply branched covers, and these presentations can be deformed alongside the underlying bundles. The relative Picard description yields explicit local dimension formulas and recovers the stack of regular Higgs bundles as base change along the Hitchin base. We also characterise the additional data supplied to a spectral structure by a regular Higgs field as a global twisted generator, and prove that every vector bundle of rank at least three admits smooth connected simply branched spectral structures which cannot arise from any Higgs field.
item.dc:creator: Nikita Nikolaev
